title: Benny Green and the copied solo
summary: He says trombonist Benny Green copied his solo note for note, put it in Down Beat and said he could not play.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: We've gotten a lot accomplished today. We talked a lot about your life work till about 1950, the 50's. Now I think it will just take one more sitting and we'll be able to go on up from there from the 50's up till now. Then there are just some general questions that are the things I was asking you, the feelings of other musicians, especially the feelings that your friends and the musicians from your era who played together felt about some of the younger musicians who came up after you, like you were talking about Jay Jay, and like how they felt about Charlie Parker and about the pianist Bud Powell. If you had heard there was a couple of trombonists who were around, you know, people like Benny Green. Were you familiar with Benny Green's playing?
I don't see nothing wrong with him?
(LAUGHTER) Just the way you said that! Did you like the way he played?
Yeah, but don't steal my stuff and then put in the catalog that I can't play. He played it note for note but I caught him. He was playing here at ( ? ).
Yes. I went over there one night and I told him. I said, "I got you this time."
Were you living here at that time?
Yes. It was in down beat. He said that I couldn't play.
Yeah, and copied the tune that I had written, the solo, you know. They had him to copy it and put it in the magazine.
Yeah. He said, "I didn't do it," and I said, "That's your end."
